findings.title: Forecast prose says opex grows more slowly than revenue; assumptions do not show that across the horizon
findings.detail: note.md (Guidance and outlook, Judgment) says the model lets operating expenses grow more slowly than revenue after FY2027Q3. assumptions.json opex_pct_revenue runs 0.0852, 0.0844, 0.0844, 0.0852. Opex therefore grows more slowly than revenue in FY2027Q4, at the same rate in FY2028Q1 and faster in FY2028Q2 (+8.0% opex vs +7% revenue). The exit ratio equals the starting ratio. The numbers are correct, but the sentence overstates the operating leverage assumed.
findings.required_evidence: Sentence describes opex as roughly constant at about 8.4-8.5% of revenue, or assumptions changed to match the prose

findings.title: Lead-in 'The outlook excludes China' is broader than the quote
findings.detail: Key points: 'The outlook excludes China: [[Q-2]]'. Q-2 says only that no Data Center compute revenue from China is assumed. The verbatim quote that follows corrects the scope and the later sections word it accurately, so the meaning is not changed. The lead-in could still be read as excluding all China revenue.
findings.required_evidence: Lead-in reads e.g. 'The outlook assumes no China Data Center compute revenue'

findings.title: peers.json 'calendar' label inconsistent with ttm_end (code output, not used in note)
findings.detail: numerical/recompute/peers.json labels AMD (ttm_end 2026-06-27), AVGO (2026-05-03) and MRVL (2026-05-02) as calendar 'CY2025Q4'. The TTM end dates are consistent with the note's statement that peer periods end one to three months before NVIDIA's quarter end, and the label is not rendered in the note. This is informational only: the label comes from controller code, which no generator role can fix.
findings.required_evidence: None for this candidate; code owner may review the calendar labelling
